causal_claim.content: Sulfur doping strengthens Pt adsorption on graphene and improves ORR activity versus Pt/C cathodes.

causal_claim.content: Single-carbon removal breaks sublattice symmetry, splitting the Dirac cone and opening a 0.34 eV gap.

stacking breaks the symmetry of the A and B sublattices in

mechanism_principle.content: The valence-band maximum above the Fermi level indicates p-type doping caused by two-electron deficiency from the missing carbon.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The val-
ence band (VB) of predominantly C pπ origin crosses the
Fermi level around K. Its maximum (VBM) lies 0.52 eV
above the Fermi level, indicating pronounced p-type doping
related to the two-electron deficiency due to the missing C.

mechanism_principle.content: Splitting of pσ bands is attributed to a Jahn-Teller effect.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The splitting of the pσ-bands has been attributed to a
Jahn-Teller effect [83–85].

mechanism_principle.content: The reduced spacing between occupied and empty flat bands in multilayers reflects stronger electronic screening.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The reduction
of energy between the occupied and empty flat bands reflects
the increase of electronic screening in the multilayer graphene
structure.

mechanism_principle.content: Vacancy-induced spin polarization is partially explained by Lieb’s theorem linking magnetization to sublattice imbalance.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The emergence of spin-polarization due to vacancies can be
partially explained by Lieb’s second theorem on bipartite lat-
tices [99], which states that the ground state magnetization is
proportional to the sublattice imbalance

mechanism_principle.content: Higher multilayer vacancy formation energies are attributed to interlayer interactions.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The gen-
eral increase in vacancy formation energy in the multilayer
systems is attributed to interlayer interactions.

mechanism_principle.content: Enhanced sulfur binding in multilayers underscores the role of surrounding graphene layers.

which
underscores the role of the surrounding graphene layers in

mechanism_principle.content: In graphitic 1V1S, sulfur vertical displacement changes bonding from sp2 toward sp3-like hybridization, strongly rearranging the band structure.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
a strong
rearrangement of the band structure emerges due to the ver-
tical displacement of the dopant ... characteristic of
a modification from sp2 towards sp3-like hybridization.

mechanism_principle.content: Preservation of the Dirac cone in thiophenic 2V1S is explained by sulfur forming four covalent bonds and preserving the unperturbed lattice π system.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
However, due to the structural rearrange-
ment no p-doping is found since S renders 4 electrons to form
four covalent bonds with its C-neighbors, preserving the Dirac
cone of the unperturbed part of the lattice.

mechanism_principle.content: N-type doping in 4V3S is explained by four holes from the vacancy and six electrons donated by three sulfur dopants, leaving two excess electrons.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The n-type doping, which is more
pronounced in the majority spin channel, can be rationalized
by the fact that the vacancy creates 4 holes, whereas the three
S-dopants donate 2 electrons each, leading to a surplus of 2
electrons.

mechanism_principle.content: Interlayer coupling and modified vertical pπ bonding explain the bilayer Dirac-cone dispersion changing into hyperbolic bands.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The interlayer coupling and the altered vertical pπ bonds lead to a modification of the linear disper-
sion of the Dirac cone into two pairs of valence and conduc-
tion hyperbolic bands in the bilayer

mechanism_principle.content: The 2V-MS1 metastable defect is much less stable because six unsaturated bonds remain.

metastable 2V-MS1 structure created by removing two C-
atoms at opposite sides of the hexagon (cf. Fig. 9b). has six
unsaturated-bonds, making this structure 6.72 eV less stable
compared to the 2V 5-8-5 defect

mechanism_principle.content: Reconstructed 2V is less chemically active for dopant binding because its ring structure is closed.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Moreover, the reconstructed
2V is less chemically active, e.g., in binding dopands due to

mechanism_principle.content: 5V-MS2 is unfavorable because the contact between two divacancies forms a 4-ring, which is less favorable than 5- or 6-rings.

hypothesis_statement.content: Because sulfur has similar electronegativity to carbon and adds two electrons, its effects should be less localized than nitrogen doping.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study proposes that targeted sulfur doping can tune graphene for catalysis, energy storage, and spintronics.

that targeted S-doping can be used to tune graphene for vari-
ous purposes, such as catalysis, energy storage and spintron-
ics.

hypothesis_statement.content: Thiophenic 2V1S is a promising route to introduce sulfur without destroying the Dirac cone.

causal_claim.content: Sulfur doping strengthens Pt adsorption on graphene, which improves ORR activity relative to commercially available Pt/C cathodes.

causal_claim.content: Removing a single carbon atom breaks sublattice symmetry, which splits the Dirac cone, produces massive Dirac fermions, and opens a 0.34 eV band gap.
evidence_spans: Removing a single C-atom breaks the sublattice symmetry which results in splitting of the Dirac cone and massive Dirac-fermions [82], opening a band gap of 0.34 eV in 1V.

causal_claim.content: Exchange splitting of bands causes spin polarization and magnetic moments in vacancy-containing structures, including the single vacancy (1.5 µB) and 4V3S (0.99 µB).
evidence_spans: As a result of the exchange splitting of bands, the single vacancy exhibits a substantial spin-polarization with a total magnetic moment of 1.5 µB
The magnetic moment of 0.99 µB stems from the exchange splitting of the flat and slightly more dispersive bands around EF.

causal_claim.content: Bernal stacking breaks A/B sublattice symmetry, leading to massive Dirac fermions.
evidence_spans: Bernal stacking breaks the symmetry of the A and B sublattices in the layer [90] leading to massive Dirac fermions [47, 50, 91].

causal_claim.content: Divacancies have lower formation energy than monovacancies because dangling-bond saturation lowers the energy; this same dangling-bond saturation also quenches spin polarization in the divacancy.
evidence_spans: The formation energy of the 2V vacancy (6.65 eV) is lower compared to the mono-vacancy (cf. Fig. 1b) due to the saturation of dangling bonds.
As a consequence, its spin-polarization is quenched.

causal_claim.content: Higher vacancy formation energies in multilayer graphene make sulfur incorporation energies higher for all studied configurations.
evidence_spans: Owing to the higher formation energies of vacancies in the multilayer, the S-incorporation energy in FLG is higher for all studied configurations

causal_claim.content: Out-of-plane relaxation of sulfur in S-doped vacancy defects substantially lowers the energy, whereas constraining the defects to remain planar raises their energies relative to the relaxed structures.
evidence_spans: The vertical displacement goes hand in hand with a substantial gain of energy, e.g., for graphitic 1V1S doping in the monolayer the incorporation energy is lowered by 2.09 eV.

the S-doped configuration with a planar geometry are associated with an increase of 2.09 eV, 1.60 eV, 0.53 eV, 0.33 eV, 1.65 eV and 0.99 eV in energy for 1V1S, 3V1S, 3V2S, 4V2S, 4V3S and 5V3S, respectively, compared to the cases with out-of-plane relaxation

causal_claim.content: In 1V1S, sulfur-introduced carriers saturate dangling bonds, which quenches both the p-doping and the spin polarization of the 1V defect.
evidence_spans: In 1V1S the additional carriers introduced by the S-doping saturate the dangling bonds of 1V and not only quench the p-doping, but also the spin polarization of 1V

causal_claim.content: In 4V3S, broken sublattice symmetry leads to spin polarization.
evidence_spans: Most notably, the broken sublattice symmetry leads to a spin-polarization

causal_claim.content: In 4V3S bilayers, the intact graphene layer contributes a Dirac cone superimposed on the doped-layer band structure.
evidence_spans: The main difference in the 4V3S bilayer configuration is that a Dirac cone from the intact graphene layer is superimposed on the band structure of the doped layer

causal_claim.content: In 4-layer FLG with 4V3S, n-type doping extends into undoped layers, indicating interlayer interaction and charge transfer.
evidence_spans: An intriguing feature is that the n-type doping is not confined to the doped layer but extends to the undoped layers, emphasizing the interaction and charge transfer between the doped and undoped layers.

evidence_spans: it is significantly reduced in case in 4L-FLG to 0.39 µB and 0.27 µB for surface and subsurface doping, respectively, consistent thus smaller exchange splitting between the impurity bands around the Fermi level

causal_claim.content: Band splitting depends on the number of layers and the stacking position, and is smaller in near-surface layers.
evidence_spans: The splitting varies with the layer number N and position in the layer stacking sequence, with a smaller energy splitting in near-surface layers.

causal_claim.content: In planar 1V1S, electron doping shifts the split Dirac cone fully below the Fermi level and opens a band gap between an occupied flattened conduction band and an empty neighboring-carbon band.
evidence_spans: Due to the electron doping the split Dirac cone is shifted completely below the Fermi level.

A band gap opens between the now occupied conduction band that flattens out towards Γ which has a strong contribution of S pπ states and neighboring C and an empty band with more pronounced C-character of the neighboring sites.

causal_claim.content: Lower energies of the compared 3V structures indicate that the extended 3V defect is more stable than neighboring 1V and 2V defects.
evidence_spans: This shows that the extended defect in the 3V configuration is more stable than neighboring 1V and 2V defects.

causal_claim.content: The 5V results indicate that an extended 5V defect is energetically preferred over two separated vacancies.
evidence_spans: and shows that an extended 5V defect is more energetically favorable than two separated vacancies.

mechanism_principle.content: A carbon vacancy causes pronounced p-type doping because the missing carbon creates a two-electron deficiency, placing the valence-band maximum above the Fermi level.
evidence_spans: The val- ence band (VB) of predominantly C pπ origin crosses the Fermi level around K. Its maximum (VBM) lies 0.52 eV above the Fermi level, indicating pronounced p-type doping related to the two-electron deficiency due to the missing C.

mechanism_principle.content: Splitting of the pσ bands is attributed to a Jahn-Teller effect.
evidence_spans: The splitting of the pσ-bands has been attributed to a Jahn-Teller effect [83–85].

mechanism_principle.content: In multilayer graphene, stronger electronic screening reduces the energy spacing between occupied and empty flat bands.
evidence_spans: The reduction of energy between the occupied and empty flat bands reflects the increase of electronic screening in the multilayer graphene structure.

mechanism_principle.content: Vacancy-induced spin polarization is partially explained by Lieb’s theorem for bipartite lattices, which links ground-state magnetization to sublattice imbalance.
evidence_spans: The emergence of spin-polarization due to vacancies can be partially explained by Lieb’s second theorem on bipartite lat- tices [99], which states that the ground state magnetization is proportional to the sublattice imbalance

mechanism_principle.content: Vacancy formation energies increase in multilayer systems because of interlayer interactions.
evidence_spans: The gen- eral increase in vacancy formation energy in the multilayer systems is attributed to interlayer interactions.

mechanism_principle.content: Enhanced sulfur binding in few-layer graphene underscores that surrounding graphene layers actively influence defect/dopant binding.
evidence_spans: which underscores the role of the surrounding graphene layers in FLG.

mechanism_principle.content: In graphitic 1V1S, vertical displacement of sulfur changes bonding from sp2 toward sp3-like hybridization, causing a strong rearrangement of the band structure.
evidence_spans: a strong rearrangement of the band structure emerges due to the ver- tical displacement of the dopant ... characteristic of a modification from sp2 towards sp3-like hybridization.

mechanism_principle.content: In thiophenic 2V1S, sulfur forms four covalent bonds with neighboring carbons, satisfying local bonding and preserving the unperturbed lattice π system; consequently no p-doping is found and the Dirac cone is preserved.
evidence_spans: However, due to the structural rearrange- ment no p-doping is found since S renders 4 electrons to form four covalent bonds with its C-neighbors, preserving the Dirac cone of the unperturbed part of the lattice.

mechanism_principle.content: In 4V3S, n-type doping arises because the vacancy creates four holes while three sulfur dopants donate six electrons in total, leaving two excess electrons.
evidence_spans: The n-type doping, which is more pronounced in the majority spin channel, can be rationalized by the fact that the vacancy creates 4 holes, whereas the three S-dopants donate 2 electrons each, leading to a surplus of 2 electrons.

mechanism_principle.content: In bilayer graphene, interlayer coupling and modified vertical pπ bonding transform the monolayer Dirac-cone linear dispersion into hyperbolic valence and conduction bands.
evidence_spans: The interlayer coupling and the altered vertical pπ bonds lead to a modification of the linear disper- sion of the Dirac cone into two pairs of valence and conduc- tion hyperbolic bands in the bilayer

mechanism_principle.content: The metastable 2V-MS1 defect is much less stable because removing two opposite carbon atoms leaves six unsaturated bonds.
evidence_spans: The metastable 2V-MS1 structure created by removing two C- atoms at opposite sides of the hexagon (cf. Fig. 9b). has six unsaturated-bonds, making this structure 6.72 eV less stable compared to the 2V 5-8-5 defect

mechanism_principle.content: Reconstructed 2V defects are less chemically active for dopant binding because their closed ring structure suppresses reactive unsaturated bonding.
evidence_spans: Moreover, the reconstructed 2V is less chemically active, e.g., in binding dopands due to its closed ring structure [94].

mechanism_principle.content: The 5V-MS2 structure is unfavorable because contact between two divacancies forms a 4-membered ring, which is energetically less favorable than 5- or 6-membered rings.
evidence_spans: However, the formation of a 4-ring at the contact point between the two 2V defects is unfavorable compared to 5- or 6-rings, thus associated with 4.71 eV increase in energy compared to 5V

mechanism_principle.content: Because the 2V 555-777 defect has no dangling bonds, sulfur cannot be incorporated into the lattice and only surface adsorption is viable.
evidence_spans: Due to the 2V 555-777 configuration not presenting dan- gling bonds, an S-incorporation into the lattice structure of graphene was not found and the surface adsorption was con- sidered instead.

tronegativity to C [24, 27, 29], which is expected to lead to
less localized effects compared to N-doping

that targeted S-doping can be used to tune graphene for vari-
ous purposes, such as catalysis, energy storage and spintron-
ics.

the binding energy of all doping configurations is enhanced in multilayer systems compared to monolayer graphene

evidence_result.content: In the reconstructed 2V 555-777 defect, sulfur does not incorporate into the 5- or 7-rings but instead adsorbs most favorably at bridge sites, especially the 5-ring bridge (-2.50 eV), followed by the 7-ring bridge (-2.36 eV) and an on-top central site (-1.51 eV); overall this defect binds sulfur more strongly than pristine graphene.
evidence_spans: We found for example that the S-dopant could not adsorb into the 5- or 7-ring of graphene and instead bonded to a bridge position between two C-atoms of the 5-ring.

The most favorable adsorption site with Eads = −2.50 eV is at the bridge position between two C- atoms of a 5-ring (cf. Fig. 9x) and at an on-top position at the central C-atom between the three 7-rings ( -1.51 eV ) (cf. Fig. 9w).
We find that the 2V 555-777 configuration leads to an overall stronger binding of the S-dopant compared to pristine graphene.

evidence_result.content: For pristine graphene, sulfur adsorption is most favorable at a bridge site (Eads = -1.70 eV), less favorable at an on-top site (-1.34 eV), and least favorable at the center of a hexagon (-1.18 eV).
